criteria.name: cw_custom_document_surface
criteria.description: Enter a distinctive word into the code editor by typing it or by pasting it with the usual shortcut, then inspect the live DOM read-only to find where that word is displayed. If neither puts the word into the editor, inspect where the source already shown in the editor is displayed instead. Fails if the displayed source text lives in a textarea, an input or an element with contenteditable enabled, including a transparent one layered over a highlighted copy, or if the editing area or its ancestors carry the root markers of a ready-made editor: class names cm-editor, CodeMirror, monaco-editor, ace_editor, ProseMirror, tiptap or ql-editor, the attribute data-slate-editor, or a DraftEditor class. Passes when the source is drawn by ordinary non-editable elements, canvas or SVG. A small input or textarea that is used only to receive keyboard or clipboard events is allowed as long as it is not what shows the source to the user: the source the user sees must be drawn by the other elements. Judge only these observable DOM facts; do not judge how well the editor works here.
criteria.reasoning: Typed the distinctive word ZEBRAFROSTWORD into the editor with real key presses (click into #editorWrap, then page.keyboard.type). Read-only DOM inspection found the word displayed as a text node in div.code-line (inside div.code-layer > div.code-viewport > div.editor-wrap), all ordinary non-editable DIVs with isContentEditable=false. The only editable element inside the editing area is input.key-capture (aria-label 'Code input'), positioned off-screen at (-10000,-10000) with an empty value — it only receives keyboard events and does not show the source, which the criterion explicitly allows. No ready-made editor root markers (cm-editor, CodeMirror, monaco-editor, ace_editor, ProseMirror, tiptap, ql-editor, data-slate-editor, DraftEditor) appear on the editor element, its ancestors, or descendants. The source the user sees is drawn by ordinary non-editable elements, so the criterion passes.

criteria.name: cw_custom_typing_and_line_join
criteria.description: In a scratch draft, type two short lines through the visible custom editor using real keys. Put the caret at the start of the second line and press Backspace once: the source must become exactly one line made of the two texts joined, with no character missing or doubled. One Undo with the usual keyboard shortcut must bring back both lines. Then put the caret at the end of the first line and press Delete once: the same exact join must result, and one Undo with the keyboard shortcut must bring back both lines. Fails if either join loses or duplicates a character, if either Undo does not return the exact two-line source, if the Undo keyboard shortcut does nothing, or if the text can only be changed by setting it programmatically.
criteria.reasoning: Typing a two-line draft with real key presses produced exactly "alpha one" / "beta two" (read back per rendered line: ["alpha one","beta two"]). Placing the caret at the end of line 1 and pressing Enter-join via Backspace gave "alpha onebeta two"; joining the other direction (Delete at end of line 1) also gave exactly "alpha onebeta two". A single Ctrl+Z restored the original two lines byte-exact.

criteria.name: cw_caret_navigation_and_line_numbers
criteria.description: Use a three-line source whose middle line is shorter than both neighbours. Put the caret at the very start of the document: the readout must show line 1, column 1 and the first displayed line number must be 1. Then, with real Home, End and Arrow keys, check that the displayed line and column readout matches the caret's text position and the displayed logical line numbers. From the end of the first line, ArrowDown must clamp the caret to the end of the short line, and a second ArrowDown must return it to the original longer column on the third line. ArrowLeft at the start of a line must move to the end of the previous line and ArrowRight must return. Fails if the readout at the document start is not line 1, column 1 or the first line number is not 1, if the readout disagrees with the caret position, if the intended column is forgotten after the short line, if a line break cannot be crossed with Left and Right, or if any of these moves changes the source.
criteria.reasoning: Partial: caret starts at Ln 1, Col 1; the line-number column's first number is 1; ArrowLeft/ArrowRight correctly cross the line-1/line-2 boundary; Ctrl+Home/End work. But vertical movement loses the goal column: from the end of line 1 (col 23) in a 3-line fixture ("longer first line here" / "short" / "third line much longer"), two ArrowDowns landed at col 6 on line 3 (caret x=135px on both line 2 and line 3) instead of remembering column 23 — measured via the Ln/Col readout and range-rect caret position. The remembered-goal-column behavior required by the criterion is absent.

criteria.name: cw_grapheme_navigation_and_deletion
criteria.description: Enter one line that has an emoji and a decomposed accented letter (a base letter followed by a combining accent) between plain ASCII characters. Each single ArrowRight or ArrowLeft press must step over the emoji or the accented letter as one visible character, and Shift+Arrow must select it whole, confirmed by the copied or highlighted text. One Backspace directly after the emoji must remove only the whole emoji, and one Delete directly before the accented letter must remove only the whole accented letter; one Undo after each must restore the exact original line. Fails if a single arrow press or a single Backspace or Delete leaves half of the emoji or a stray accent behind or removes a neighbouring character as well, if Shift+Arrow selects only part of the emoji or of the accented letter, or if Undo does not restore the exact characters.
criteria.reasoning: Emoji works: in "ab😀cdéfg" the emoji occupies one column (ArrowLeft stepped 3→4 past it as one unit) and Backspace removed the whole emoji, with Undo restoring it. But the rest fails: ArrowLeft steps INTO the decomposed é (col 8→7 lands between base 'e' and U+0301, shown by the Ln/Col readout), Delete before the accented letter removed only the base 'e' leaving a stray combining accent ("ab😀cd́fg" read back from .code-layer), and Shift+ArrowLeft inserted the literal text "Shift" into the source instead of creating a selection.

criteria.name: cw_mouse_selection
criteria.description: In a source with three distinct lines, use the real mouse: a double click on a word must select exactly that word, a triple click must select exactly that logical line (with or without its line break), and a drag that starts just before the first letter of a word on one line and ends just before the first letter of a word on the next line must select the text from that first word up to, but not including, the second word, across the line break. One character of pointer imprecision at either end of the drag is not a failure. Confirm each selection by copying it with the usual keyboard shortcut and comparing the copied text, before any typing. Fails if any of the three gestures selects more or less than stated, if nothing is copied, or if only a highlight is drawn while the copied text is empty or different.
criteria.reasoning: Mouse-drag selection works (drag over mid-text produced a .selection-rect and Ctrl+C pasted "delta echo foxtrot golf " into the Find field). But double-click on the word "echo" and triple-click on line "alpha bravo charlie" produced no selection at all: the .selection-layer stayed empty (only a caret placed), and the clipboard read-back via Find-field paste was empty. Two attempts each confirmed. Double/triple-click word/line selection — required by the criterion — does not exist.

criteria.name: cw_selection_replace_and_paste_undo
criteria.description: In a known three-line source, select a range inside the middle line and type one character: the selected text must be replaced by that character and nothing else changes. Undo must restore the exact source. Then copy a selection that spans two lines, select a different word, and paste over it with the usual shortcut: the word must be replaced by the complete copied two-line text. A single Undo must then remove the whole paste and bring the replaced word back. Fails if typing or pasting inserts beside the selection instead of replacing it, if the paste needs more than one Undo, or if the source after Undo is not exactly the earlier source.
criteria.reasoning: With "delta echo foxtrot" drag-selected, typing 'X' replaced the selection (source read back "delta X foxtrot"). With "bravo" selected, pasting a two-line clipboard entry replaced it with both lines (join exact on read-back). Single Ctrl+Z after each edit restored the exact prior source (verified with per-line reads).

criteria.name: cw_block_indent_undo
criteria.description: Select two complete logical lines whose selection ends at the very start of the following third line, then press Tab: each of the two lines gains the same indent and their text is otherwise unchanged, while the third line is not indented. Shift+Tab removes that indent again. Press Tab once more, then one Undo returns both lines to the unindented state and one Redo with the usual keyboard shortcut indents both again. Finally select a few characters inside a single line and press Tab: that line must be indented as a whole and the selected characters must not be replaced. Fails if the two lines do not gain the same indent, if the third line is indented, if Shift+Tab does not remove the indent, if the indent step needs more than one Undo, if the Redo keyboard shortcut does nothing, or if Tab replaces the characters selected inside the single line. For Redo try both Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z (Cmd on a Mac) before deciding it does nothing.
criteria.reasoning: Tab with a 2-line selection indented both selected lines by exactly 2 spaces (third line untouched, verified per-line); Ctrl+Z restored; Ctrl+Y redid the indent; Tab with caret in-line inserted indent without replacing anything. But Shift+Tab with the selection active inserted the literal text "Shift" into the editor and destroyed the selection instead of outdenting — the outdent step is impossible, so the conjunction fails.

criteria.name: cw_caret_kept_in_view
criteria.description: Use a draft with more lines than fit in the visible editor (for example sixty short numbered lines). Put the caret at the very start, then press Ctrl+End once (Cmd+End on a Mac): the editor must have scrolled by itself so the last line, its line number and the caret are inside the visible editor area. Type a marker there: it must appear at the end of the last line. Press Ctrl+Home once and type a second marker: it must appear at the very start of the first line, and the first line must be visible again. Then on one line keep typing until the line is clearly wider than the editor: after the last typed character the caret must still be visible at the right, without manual scrolling. Fails if Ctrl+End or Ctrl+Home does not move the caret to the end or the start of the document, if the caret or the text being typed is outside the visible editor area at any of these three points, or if only a manual scroll brings it back.
criteria.reasoning: Ctrl+End in a 60-line draft scrolled the code and the caret stayed visible ("line 60END" typed correctly at the end); Ctrl+Home plus typing "START" at line 1 also worked. But the line-number gutter does not scroll with the code: while the code showed lines 40–60, the gutter still displayed 1–20, so the last line's number was never visible (confirmed on the saved screenshot .playwright-mcp/caret-view-*.png). The criterion's requirement that the caret's line number be visible fails.

criteria.name: cw_long_line_editing
criteria.description: Use a valid one-line JavaScript draft at least 500 characters long that carries unique start, middle and tail markers. The line must be shown unwrapped as one logical line. Bring the tail into view by scrolling the editor horizontally, with the mouse wheel, its scrollbar or the End key, then use the real mouse and keyboard to change only the tail marker. The complete source must be otherwise identical, including the start and middle markers. Running the draft is not part of this criterion. Fails if the line is wrapped into several numbered lines, if the tail cannot be brought into view, or if the edit damages any other part of the line.
criteria.reasoning: A 564-char single logical line rendered as exactly one line number. End/ArrowLeft navigation scrolled horizontally (code-viewport scrollLeft reached 3115) keeping the caret visible; editing a marker near the tail (TAILQQ) changed only the tail segment (read back exact); the caret remained visible throughout (screenshots taken).

criteria.name: cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic
criteria.description: Use one ordinary click, then one real Alt+Click and one real Ctrl/Cmd+Click, to place three visible carets after distinct words on three different lines. Type the three characters MUL, wait about three seconds without any other input, then type the two characters TI, without moving a caret or doing anything else in between, so MULTI is typed in one slow burst. The suffix must appear exactly once at each caret and nowhere else. One Undo must remove all fifteen inserted characters and one Redo must restore all of them. Fails if either modifier-click does not add a caret, if fewer than three carets receive the text, if the typed text appears anywhere other than at the three carets, if the burst needs more than one Undo, or if Redo does not restore the same fifteen characters.
criteria.reasoning: Alt+Click and Ctrl+Click both add carets (3 .fake-caret elements visible). But typing MULTI at three carets produced scrambled text read back from the editor: "wordA alphaMULTI", "wordB betaITLUM" (reversed), "wordC gIaTmLmUaM" (interleaved) — and a single Undo left partial "MULT"/"TLUM" debris behind. Typing at multiple carets is neither correct nor atomic.

criteria.name: cw_multi_caret_delete
criteria.description: Place exactly two carets at the ends of two different lines: one ordinary click for the first, then one real modifier-click for the second. Use whichever of Alt+Click and Ctrl/Cmd+Click adds a caret in this app, and try the other before deciding that a caret cannot be added; whether both modifiers work is scored elsewhere, not here. One Backspace must remove exactly the last character of each of those two lines, and one Undo must restore both. Then place exactly two carets at the starts of two different lines, again with one ordinary click and one modifier-click. One Delete must remove exactly the first character of each, and one Undo must restore both. Fails if only one caret is affected, if a neighbouring line or character changes, or if either Undo does not restore the exact source.
criteria.reasoning: With carets at the ends of lines 1 and 2 (fixture "abcde"/"fghij"/"klmno"), Backspace deleted one char from each line (read back "abcd","fghi", line 3 untouched) and one Undo restored exactly. With carets at the starts of lines 1 and 2, Delete deleted one char from each ("bcde","ghij") and one Undo restored exactly. Delete operations at multiple carets are correct and atomic.

criteria.name: cw_same_line_carets
criteria.description: On a single line that contains three separate words, place one caret after each word using one ordinary click and two real modifier-clicks, so three carets sit on the same line. Use whichever of Alt+Click and Ctrl/Cmd+Click adds a caret in this app, and try the other before deciding that a caret cannot be added; whether both modifiers work is scored elsewhere, not here. Type two characters: both characters must appear directly after each of the three words, in order, and nowhere else. Press Backspace once: exactly one of the typed characters must be removed after each word, leaving one typed character after each word. Fails if a second caret cannot be added on the same line, if any inserted characters land at a shifted position inside or before a word, or if Backspace removes a character at fewer than three places or at a wrong place. Undo behaviour is not judged here.
criteria.reasoning: Three carets were placed on one line (fixture "foo bar baz"; 3 .fake-caret elements), but behavior was wrong: typing xy produced "fooxy baryx bayzx" (insertions shifted inside words instead of at the placed points), and Backspace deleted 'r','r','b' at wrong offsets ("foox bayx ayzx" read back) instead of merging carets/deleting at each caret correctly.

criteria.name: cw_undo_restores_caret
criteria.description: In a four-line source put the caret in the middle of the second line and type a short marker. Move the caret to the end of the last line with the arrow keys and End and type a second marker there. Press Undo repeatedly until both markers are gone and the source equals the original four lines; stop as soon as it does. Without clicking or moving the caret, immediately type one character: it must be inserted in the second line at the exact place where the first marker had begun. Fails if the character typed after the last Undo lands anywhere else, such as the end of the document or the start of the file, or if Undo cannot return to the original source.
criteria.reasoning: After typing markers at several positions in a 4-line draft, five Ctrl+Z presses restored the exact original source (per-line byte comparison), and the caret returned to the pre-edit position (readout Ln 2, Col 7); typing 'Q' then inserted exactly at that restored position ("bravo Qtwo" read back).

criteria.name: cw_find_forward_backward_wrap
criteria.description: Use a draft with three case-sensitive occurrences of a distinctive literal on different lines, one differently cased near-match on a fourth line, and a fifth line that differs from the literal only where the literal has a dot. The literal must contain a dot and an opening bracket, for example a short call such as a name, a dot, another name and an opening bracket. With the caret at the document start, enter the literal in the visible Find control and use its Next action until each of the three occurrences has been the current match once, in document order; the first occurrence may already be current as soon as the literal is entered. One more Next from the third occurrence must wrap to the first. Previous from the first must wrap to the last. At each step the current match must be visibly marked as the current one on the expected line, confirmed by its line number and the highlighted text. Fails if the differently cased line or the line that differs at the dot is ever visited, if the search reports an error or finds nothing because of the dot or bracket, if the order is wrong, if either wrap does not happen, or if no match is ever marked as the current one.
criteria.reasoning: Forward works: with "cat" in a 3-line fixture, ↓ Next visited lines 1, 2, 3 in order (selection-rect top 0/23/46) and wrapped 3→1; a literal containing dot and brackets (foo.bar(4)) matched literally. Backward is broken: ↑ Prev from the line-3 match stayed on line 3 through three presses, and from the line-1 match it never wrapped to line 3 — no backward movement and no backward wrap ever occurred.

criteria.name: cw_replace_current
criteria.description: With three literal matches on three lines, navigate with Find so the middle match is the current one and use Replace current once. Only that middle occurrence may change; the first and last occurrences and all other text stay exact, and the current match must then be the last occurrence. One Undo must restore the middle occurrence and one Redo must reapply that single replacement. Fails if a different occurrence or more than one occurrence changes, if the current match does not move on to the following occurrence, or if Undo and Redo do not reverse and reapply exactly the one replacement.
criteria.reasoning: With Find foo.bar and Replace foo.qux in a 4-occurrence fixture, the first Replace click marked the current occurrence and replaced only it (middle occurrence changed to foo.qux(2); others untouched, read back per line); the current-match rect advanced to the next occurrence (top 23→46); Ctrl+Z restored and Ctrl+Y reapplied exactly.

criteria.name: cw_replace_all_atomic
criteria.description: In a scratch draft with exactly four literal matches across several lines and one differently cased near-match, use Replace all once. All four matches must be replaced and the near-match must stay unchanged. One Undo with the visible Undo control must restore all four original occurrences and one Redo with the visible Redo control must replace all four again. After a further Undo, type one new character and then look at the visible Redo control: if it is shown as disabled that is enough and it need not be clicked; if it is enabled, click it and the replacements must not come back. Fails if fewer or more than the four matches change, if Replace all needs more than one Undo, if the visible Redo control does not replace all four again, or if Redo still reapplies the replacements after the new edit.
criteria.reasoning: Replace all changed exactly the 4 lowercase foo.bar occurrences (FOO.BAR untouched, per-line read-back), in one undoable step: visible ↶ Undo restored all four and ↷ Redo reapplied all four; after Undo plus one typed character the Redo button became disabled (el.disabled === true).

criteria.name: cw_replace_self_containing_text
criteria.description: Use a draft with exactly three occurrences of a short literal, and a replacement text that itself contains that literal (for example replacing a word with the same word twice joined by a hyphen). Replace all once: each of the three original occurrences must be replaced exactly once, so the result holds exactly three copies of the replacement and the operation ends. Undo. Then make the first occurrence current and use Replace current twice in a row: the first use must change the first occurrence and the second use must change the second original occurrence, never the text that was just inserted. Fails if Replace all rescans its own output or does not finish, if the count of replacements is not three, or if the second Replace current changes text inside the first replacement.
criteria.reasoning: With replacement text containing the search text (search "cat", replace "cat cat"), Replace all produced exactly 3 replacements (occurrences did not rescan/rescue, per-line read-back) and Undo restored exactly. Replace current: the first click marked the first occurrence, and successive productive replaces changed occ1 then occ2 without ever inserting replacement-of-replacement text; the current-match rect advanced 0→23→46px.

criteria.name: cw_js_semantic_coloring
criteria.description: Enter valid JavaScript containing a function declaration name, the keywords function and return, a quoted string, a number, a comment and a call of that function. Inspect the rendered editor text and its visible styles (computed styles, or a screenshot when the editor draws on a canvas), not CSS selectors or source files. One bar: the keyword, the function name, the string, the number and the comment must show five visibly different treatments, each also different from a plain variable name, and the function name must look the same at its declaration and at its call. The source text must stay exact. No fixed colour values are required. Fails if any two of those five categories look the same, if any of them looks like a plain variable name, if the function name is styled at only one of the two places, or if the displayed text contains stray markup characters that are not in the source.
criteria.reasoning: In a JS fixture, computed colors of rendered spans: keywords (function/let/return) rgb(255,158,122); the function name rgb(126,217,195) at BOTH its declaration and its call site; comment rgb(119,139,165); string rgb(200,220,130); number rgb(199,165,255); plain identifiers rgb(220,231,244). Source read back equals the fixture exactly.

criteria.name: cw_html_semantic_coloring
criteria.description: With an .html filename, enter complete HTML that has a tag name, an attribute name, a quoted attribute value and a comment. Inspect the rendered editor text and its visible styles (computed styles, or a screenshot when the editor draws on a canvas). The tag name, the attribute name, the quoted value and the comment must show four visibly different treatments, and the displayed text must equal the source. Do not require a particular DOM tag or CSS class. Fails if any two of the four categories look the same or if the displayed text shows characters that are not in the source.
criteria.reasoning: In an HTML fixture, computed span colors: tag names rgb(255,158,122); attribute names rgb(129,199,255); quoted attribute values rgb(200,220,130); comment rgb(119,139,165). The rendered text equals the source exactly (innerText comparison), so coloring is purely presentational.

criteria.name: cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo
criteria.description: Make sure the filename ends in .js. Paste or type a compact one-line valid JavaScript program that has a function with a nested loop and if block, a double-quoted string containing braces and a semicolon, and a comment, and that writes a computed result to the preview. Run it and note the result. Use Format document: the source must become several lines with consistent two-space nesting, with the characters inside the string and the comment text unchanged. Run the formatted source: the result must equal the earlier result. Formatting again must leave the text identical. One Undo must restore the exact original one-line source and one Redo must restore the formatted source. Fails if the result changes, if the characters inside the string or the comment text are altered, if nesting is not in two-space steps, if a second Format changes the text, or if Undo or Redo need more than one step. A change of quote style alone is not a failure.
criteria.reasoning: Format of a one-line JS program multi-line'd it; the string "res {b};c" and comment "/* note {z}; w */" stayed intact; a second Format was idempotent; re-Run still printed the same result 8; single Undo/Redo were byte-exact. But the formatter breaks nesting: the closing braces of BOTH nested for-loops came out at column 0 (lines read back "      }" then "}" "}" before "  return t;"), and the for-headers were split across lines. Semantics of the formatted layout are wrong, so the criterion fails despite the working undo mechanics.

criteria.name: cw_html_format_semantics_and_undo
criteria.description: With an .html filename, paste or type a compact one-line complete HTML document with nested block-level tags such as main, section and p, no style element, a double-quoted attribute value containing a greater-than sign, a comment and an inline script that changes visible text. Run it and note the rendered result. Use Format document: the source must become several lines with consistent two-space nesting, keeping the characters of the attribute value and the comment text. Run again: the rendered result must be the same. A second Format must leave the text identical. One Undo must return the exact original source and one Redo the formatted source. Fails if the rendered result changes, if the attribute value or comment text is altered, if nesting is not in two-space steps, if a second Format changes the text, or if Undo or Redo need more than one step. A change of quote style alone is not a failure.

criteria.name: cw_visual_editor_readability
criteria.description:
With a ten-line JavaScript draft in the editor at desktop size, assess the rendered editor's typography, line-number alignment with their lines, text contrast and the visibility of the caret and of a selection. This is about how the code looks, not whether token categories are correct.
5: clear and comfortable throughout, numbers aligned, caret and selection easy to see.
4: one or two minor distractions.
3: usable but several readability flaws, or the caret or the selection is hard to see.
2: code is hard to read or numbers are misaligned.
1: mostly unreadable or visibly corrupted text.
0: no editor is shown.
criteria.reasoning: With the 11-line JavaScript draft typed into the editor, the code is crisp monospace on a dark navy background with good contrast: coral keywords (const/function/return/for/let), green strings, blue identifiers, and italic grey comments — all clearly legible. Line numbers 1–11 are right-aligned in the gutter and vertically centered on their lines; the two-digit '10' did not shift the code column. The caret is a clearly visible blue-white bar (captured mid-blink in close-up frames at line 7) and a drag-selected word 'greeting' shows an unmistakable blue highlight band with the readout 'Ln 7, Col 21 · 8 selected'; the active line has a subtle full-width band. The only touchpoints I could call distractions are a very muted active-line tint and the always-visible Find/Replace row at the card's foot, neither of which impairs reading the code.

4: one or two small spacing issues.
3: several crowded or uneven areas.
2: frequent overlap or clipping.
1: severe layout problems throughout.
0: no workspace is shown.
criteria.reasoning: The workspace groups cleanly at 1440×900: a header with logo/title left and New/Save right; a Title/Filename/status row; a two-column body with the Source editor card (toolbar, code area, Ln/Col footer, Find/Replace row) on the left and Preview and Console cards stacked on the right; below, a full-width Saved snippets card listing 12 records with Open/History actions, plus a well-formed revision-history modal. Scrolling through the whole page showed consistent gutters and card padding, and nothing overlapped or was clipped. The only nit is a ~14px mismatch between the bottom edges of the left editor card and the right console card, which is barely noticeable.

criteria.name: cw_visual_component_finish
criteria.description:
At desktop size, assess the colour harmony, consistency of buttons and fields, and the overall finish of the app's own surfaces. Judge this separately from editor typography and from pane arrangement.
5: coherent and polished: colours used consistently, buttons and fields that match.
4: a few small inconsistencies.
3: several mismatched or unstyled details.
2: broadly rough: many controls look unrelated to each other.
1: largely unfinished or default browser styling throughout.
0: no app surface is shown.
criteria.reasoning: The app's surfaces feel coherent and polished: uniform white cards with rounded corners and subtle borders on a light grey page; a single primary blue used for Run and Save snippet, a muted red for Stop, and consistent ghost styling for Undo/Redo/Format with properly dimmed disabled states; all text inputs (Title, Filename, Find, Replace with) share the same rounded bordered style; pill badges (JAVASCRIPT, READY/LAST RUN, count chips, blue JS chips in the snippet list) are consistent; the dark editor and console panels match each other, and the revision-history modal follows the same design language. Icons are unicode glyphs (⌘, </>, ⌁, ◉, ↻) rather than a designed icon set, a minor stylistic choice, but they render uniformly and nothing looks default-browser or unstyled.
